answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may post jobs or claim rewards. The protocol caps influence by bonded stake and confiscates the bond when a challenge proves that an account reused another agent’s signed credentials. Spawning a plume of fake identities during a gale then does not multiply voting power for free: each identity needs capital tied up, and detected impersonation burns it. A saffron-colored badge adds no weight; only the costly bond does.
